correctness.rationale: Re-audited the corrected /workspace/repairs/1/RESULT.md and VERIFICATION.md. Over every field extension, rank at most one for left multiplication cuts out the union of the two sides on points, forcing block preservation or balanced exchange. Over any coefficient k-algebra, on the open where diagonal blocks are invertible, the mixed products force both off-diagonal blocks to vanish. The product submodule is a direct summand, so block preservation gives unit eigenvalues alpha,beta on its two lines; taking norms and dividing by the units r,s makes beta=alpha², alpha=beta². Dividing each side block by its scalar gives an isometry on the nondegenerate complement and conversely. The diagonal open and, in the balanced case, its disjoint exchange translate cover all scheme points by the residue-field argument. Thus this determines nilpotents as well as points. Orthogonal groups and the constant exchange scheme are smooth; in characteristic three z³−1=(z−1)³ and a dual-number root (1+epsilon) gives scalar derivatives (+1,−1), adding exactly one tangent dimension beyond the reduced geometric group. The original finite-field formula is mathematically consistent (the two difference-basis determinants are r and s), but is removed as a finding. A separate small K(2,2) computation reproduced orders 8,8,24 over F3,F5,F7 and tangent dimensions 1,0 in characteristics 3,5, respectively (replay /workspace/branches/51d5ccbd-3754-45f0-b3b6-bdbce7f6b1ad/independent_check.py). The frozen code was inspected, not executed; such small checks are not a scheme proof.
